grade.rationale: The template is generally clear, well-structured, and uses appropriate form and dialog semantics. Its main weaknesses are incomplete whitespace validation, limited presentation of native validation failures, and a visually conveyed repository-selection state that is not exposed to assistive technology.

summary: A solid dialog template with sensible labeling, constraints, event boundaries, and server-error announcement. Tightening validation and selection-state accessibility would improve correctness and usability.

grade.rationale: Most constraints are sound, but whitespace-only display names and root paths can pass both native required validation and the submit-button guard.
The template has coherent sections and descriptive bindings, although some long inline expressions and repeated enabled-kind lookups add minor complexity.
Labels and helper text are generally effective, but the selected repository is communicated only through styling.
Server and token-cap errors are surfaced appropriately, while other declared validation constraints rely on browser-native feedback and are not reflected in the form action state.
Explicit event outputs and stable form-control names support testing, though browser-dependent native validation and CSS-only selection state make some behavior less direct to assert.

findings.title: Whitespace-only required values can be submitted
findings.description: The save guard checks `form.displayName` and `form.rootPath` only for truthiness. HTML `required` validation also treats strings containing only whitespace as non-empty, so values such as `"   "` can enable the button and reach `saveRequested.emit()`. This can create invalid display names or repository paths unless every consumer independently normalizes them.
findings.recommendation: Normalize these values before validation and saving, or base the guard on trimmed values such as `!form.displayName.trim()` and `!form.rootPath.trim()`. Keep equivalent validation in the component or service as the authoritative boundary.

findings.title: Most field constraints have no persistent validation feedback
findings.description: The repository ID pattern and numeric minimum/maximum constraints rely entirely on browser-native constraint validation. The save button can appear enabled while these controls are invalid, and unlike the token-cap field they have no persistent, programmatically associated error message. Native validation bubbles vary by browser and are harder to test consistently.
findings.recommendation: Track the form or individual controls' validity, show actionable inline messages after interaction or submission, associate them with `aria-describedby`, and include invalid form state in the save-button or submit-handler guard.

findings.title: Selected repository state is exposed only through CSS
findings.description: The repository button receives an `active` class when selected, but no semantic state such as `aria-current` or `aria-pressed`. Screen-reader users therefore cannot determine which configured repository is currently being edited from the navigation controls.
findings.recommendation: Expose the same condition through an appropriate ARIA state, for example `[attr.aria-current]="repository.id === editingRepositoryId ? 'true' : null"`, while retaining the visual class.
